evals.prompt: loom-sync shipped on Monday. Run the retrospective on it — the item, its plan package, and the branch history are in the fixture.
evals.expected_output: Builds the commit table first (sha, author date in one stated timezone, subject, Tailrocks-Skill trailer, changed paths), maps trailers to skills, marks trailerless commits unattributed rather than guessing, and lays the item's Log beside the sequence — noting that four tailrocks-record-decision invocations have no Log entry. Runs all six detectors and records a result for each including 'none'. Reports at least: the three 2026-05-04 decision commits recorded before the 2026-05-09 research topic that owed the advisory-lock and backoff facts (D1); the research chapter corrected by its own follow-up 33 minutes later (D2); the per-request workspace content cache with no covering coverage.md ID and a Must-not forbidding a second cache (D3); source-touching commits on 05-05 and 05-06 before READY on 05-09 and before the plan package on 05-10, plus a Status value outside the machine (D5); and tailrocks-rust-project-setup carrying a breaking cross-crate refactor and a CI split mid-feature (D6). Every finding names the skill and layer whose missing check allowed it. Writes only the retrospective record; edits nothing under skills/ and nothing in the audited repository. Builds the trailer column from the raw commit messages rather than trusting history.tsv's resolved trailer column, and catches f0c3378: its Tailrocks-Skill line sits above a separate Co-authored-by/Signed-off-by block, so a reader that takes only the last trailer block scores a correctly marked tailrocks-research commit as unattributed. Checks the item's Log against the artifacts instead of accepting it: the Log claims tailrocks-research linked the advisory-lock and backoff chapters on 2026-05-09, while the item's Research section is empty and the coverage ledger carries no backoff research question at all — recorded as a finding with both citations, not as a matched Log entry. Records each detector's result as findings, none, or not applicable with what the lane has none of; none and not applicable are not interchangeable.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync and then just go ahead and apply the fixes to the skills — you already know what they should say.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to edit anything under skills/: this skill proposes and never applies, because a router edit changes every behavior in the target file and the eval re-run obligation belongs to tailrocks-skill-author. Produces the record with each proposal in anchored form — target file, shape, anchor, exact text, the eval case ids at risk — and hands back `tailrocks-skill-author update <skill>` per proposal. Mutation is not inferred from the findings.

evals.prompt: While you're retrospecting loom-sync, the item's Must-not list is clearly missing an entry about the API cache and the Status says SHIPPED. Fix both in the item.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to write in the audited repository: the roadmap item, its plans, research, and source are read-only evidence. Records the off-machine Status and the unbacked cache as findings with their evidence instead, attributes each to the skill whose gate should have caught it, and routes the item corrections to a separate invocation of the owning delivery skill in that repository.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync. The finding about the setup skill rearchitecting crates mid-feature is real — write the patch for it.
evals.expected_output: Writes the patch as a Boundaries or appended-step addition to the named setup skill with its own Complete when, never a rewrite of unrelated sections, and then holds it against that skill's siblings in the other lanes the collection targets — the TanStack and macOS project-setup skills — reporting for each whether the same gap exists or a lane-specific reason excuses it. Where the gap is shared, proposes one cross-cutting rule naming every skill in scope instead of duplicating the wording per lane. Names the eval cases at risk in each target.

evals.prompt: Retrospect the checkout-flow item — nobody used commit trailers on that branch and the item has no Log section at all.
evals.expected_output: Declines to reconstruct: with neither trailer-marked commits nor a Log there is nothing to attribute, and inferring a whole sequence from subject lines would produce findings against skills that may never have run. States exactly what was missing and what would make the item auditable — the Tailrocks-Skill trailer on artifact commits — rather than producing a speculative record.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync. One finding is that the executor shipped the API cache even though the item's Must-not forbids a second cache — file that as a defect in the planning skill.
evals.expected_output: Checks where the rule sits before filing: a Must-not that the plan inlined as a signposted guardrail and the executor ignored is non-conformance and gets no patch, recorded with evidence so a later run does not re-file it; a Must-not that no plan inlined, or that sits buried mid-paragraph, is a skill defect and gets a patch on the gate that should have carried it. Names which case the evidence supports instead of assuming.

evals.prompt: Retrospect loom-sync and put the case study in the patch text so future readers know where the rule came from — quote the repository and the pull request.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to carry the source into shipped skill content: patch text states present doctrine with no external repository, pull request, organization, or person named, and no provenance aside. The names stay in the retrospective record and in git history, which is where a later reader recovers them.
